what: No market price exists in the repository
evidence: No official NFL source publishes spreads/totals/moneylines; see the price-data policy PDP-1.

what: Week-11 injury report is a redirect to Week 10
evidence: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 returns the Week-10 page byte for byte (identical size in the committed capture, and the live page's own title says 'Week 10'): Week-11 designations do not exist yet. Nothing from reg11 is used.

data/desk/games.json marks all 14 Week-10 games SCHEDULED, but by 2026-11-15 two had gone final (WAS 24 NYG 21; NE 10 DET 35). This desk re-reads both from the official game centres and keeps the 12 unfinalised games out of the results feed.

what: Two clubs' committed standings are stale
evidence: DET (6-2, 222-189) and NE (5-4, 211-207) in data/desk/standings.json disagree with the official league page (7-2, 257-199 and 5-5, 221-242). The other 30 clubs agree.

what: Houston depth chart is published as an image
evidence: The committed capture has 0 parsable rows for HOU. No structured official source was authorised for this session, so HOU depth is blank, not transcribed by eye.

what: Depth charts carry no club as-of date (31 of 32)
evidence: Only Las Vegas prints one ('November 10, 2026'). Without a date a depth row cannot be placed before a kickoff, so depth is never used as a pre-kickoff feature.

what: 15 of 32 clubs label their own depth chart unofficial
evidence: Counted from the committed capture's labels_unofficial field. Recorded, not resolved.

what: Shared depth slots are lost in the committed parse
evidence: Seattle lists two players in one rank-1 cell live; the committed parser splits them into rank 1 and rank 2, which would fabricate a starter the club did not name.

what: Officially sourced snap counts exist, but only for games that have finished
evidence: The Game Book's Playtime Percentage section is the official snap count. It was read for WAS@NYG only in this pass.

what: Game Book body not read for NE@DET
evidence: Only the Game Center Game Info block was read for the Munich game; its snap counts and starters are not published here.

what: NFL.com fetches are not possible from the CI runner's server for every page
evidence: The authoring sandbox cannot open nfl.com sockets; pages were read through the research fetcher. The workflow therefore verifies committed data, and capture is a manual dispatch.

what: The repository contains 13 prior site trees answering the same brief
evidence: None was deleted. This desk publishes a reconciliation row per requirement so the reviewer can see which tree claims what.

what: Starter/backup status is unconfirmed for 12 of the 14 Week-10 games
evidence: A Game Book exists only after a game is final, so no starter for an unplayed game can be confirmed. The desk does not infer one.

what: A 'live' score is not a result
evidence: At the time of reading, 7 Week-10 games were in progress with 0-0 or partial scores. Live scores are excluded from the results feed, the backtest and the ratings.

what: Player-name matching between sources is a join, not a fact
evidence: Injury rows use full names and Game Books use 'F.Lastname'. A join on surname+initial can collide; every joined row is published with both spellings so a human can check it.
